QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_11

question.text: Per Chapter 9, how do most Investment Managers reconcile side-letter differential rights with their fiduciary duty to other investors?

answer.text: By disclosing every side letter in its entirety to all investors via the Investor Charter.
By creating a separate class of units with differential rights, issued to large investors.
By capping total side-letter obligations at 10% of corpus.
By routing side-letter fee concessions through a zero-coupon debenture structure.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9.4.1 states: 'To avoid such a breach of fiduciary duty, most investment managers create a separate class of units with differential rights, issued to large investors.' This converts a 'bilateral privilege' into a 'class right' with clear boundaries and disclosure. The Trap: Option A wrongly imports full-disclosure (side letters remain confidential by design). Options C and D fabricate mechanisms. Note: The separate-class-of-units approach is the workbook's recommended fiduciary-duty mitigant for differential side-letter rights.
